title: Turn the mixed numbers into improper fractions
text: $$2\frac{1}{3}$$ means $$2 + \frac{1}{3}$$, which is $$\frac{6}{3} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{7}{3}$$. A common mistake is to add the whole numbers and the fractions separately and then forget to simplify across, or to add the whole number to the denominator. $$1\frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{2}$$. What is the least common denominator of 3 and 2?

title: Rewrite $$\frac{7}{3}$$ with denominator 6
text: 3 goes into 6 twice, so the numerator 7 is multiplied by 2. What is the new numerator?

title: Rewrite $$\frac{3}{2}$$ and add
text: $$\frac{3}{2} = \frac{9}{6}$$. Add $$\frac{14}{6} + \frac{9}{6}$$. What is the numerator of the sum?

title: Worked solution
text: $$2\frac{1}{3} + 1\frac{1}{2} = \frac{7}{3} + \frac{3}{2} = \frac{14}{6} + \frac{9}{6} = \frac{23}{6}$$. Common mistake: adding the whole numbers to get 3 and the fractions to get $$\frac{2}{5}$$, then writing $$3\frac{2}{5}$$. The fraction parts did not have a common denominator, so that sum is wrong. General rule: convert mixed numbers to improper fractions, use a common denominator, then add.
